  • Method Details

    • binarySearch

      public static <T,K> int binarySearch(List<? extends T> list, K key, Comparator<? super K> comparator, Function<? super T, ? extends K> projector)
      Searches a sorted list for a key using binary search, comparing the key against a projection of each element. This is useful when elements are sorted by one of their properties and a bare key of that property's type is all that is available, which Collections.binarySearch(List, Object, Comparator) cannot do because it requires a key of the element type.

      The list must be sorted in ascending order of the projected values according to the comparator. The result is undefined if it is not. If the list contains multiple elements whose projection equals the key, there is no guarantee which one is found.

      This runs in O(log n) time for a RandomAccess list. For other lists, each probe is a List.get(int) and the search is correspondingly slower.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The element type of the list.
      K - The type of the key and of the projected element values.
      Parameters:
      list - The list to search, sorted by the projected values.
      key - The key to search for.
      comparator - The comparator that orders projected values.
      projector - A function that extracts the value to compare against the key from an element.
      Returns:
      The index of an element whose projection equals the key if one exists. Otherwise, -(insertion point) - 1, where the insertion point is the index of the first element whose projection is greater than the key, or the list size if there is none. The return value is non-negative if and only if a match is found.

    • binarySearch

      public static <T> int binarySearch(List<? extends T> list, double key, ToDoubleFunction<? super T> projector)
      Searches a sorted list for a double key using binary search, comparing the key against a projection of each element. This avoids boxing the projected values, unlike binarySearch(List, Object, Comparator, Function).

      The list must be sorted in ascending order of the projected values according to Double.compare(double, double). The result is undefined if it is not. If the list contains multiple elements whose projection equals the key, there is no guarantee which one is found.

      This runs in O(log n) time for a RandomAccess list. For other lists, each probe is a List.get(int) and the search is correspondingly slower.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The element type of the list.
      Parameters:
      list - The list to search, sorted by the projected values.
      key - The key to search for.
      projector - A function that extracts the value to compare against the key from an element.
      Returns:
      The index of an element whose projection equals the key if one exists. Otherwise, -(insertion point) - 1, where the insertion point is the index of the first element whose projection is greater than the key, or the list size if there is none. The return value is non-negative if and only if a match is found.

      The index of an element whose projection equals the key if one exists. Otherwise, -(insertion point) - 1, where the insertion point is the index of the first element whose projection is greater than the key, or the array length if there is none. The return value is non-negative if and only if a match is found.
